idea-malta.delivery: Classes with guided learning (synchronous and asynchronous) plus self-study

fondazione-doria.location: Campania, southern Italy (Fondazione Doria determines the authorised training centre)
fondazione-doria.internship: Progression toward an approximately 3-month professional internship pathway, subject to applicable conditions

idea.src: pp. 138-139 (interim exit award of the Bachelor (Honours) in Travel and Tourism)
idea.overview: A one-year MQF Level 5 diploma for students who want a practical first qualification in the travel and tourism industry. It is made up of the first six modules of IDEA College's Bachelor (Honours) in Travel and Tourism, covering tourism principles, hospitality management, travel geography and destination management alongside academic writing and critical thinking. Students can continue to the Undergraduate Higher Diploma (120 ECTS) and on to the full bachelor's degree.
who: School leavers starting a career in travel and tourism
People already working in the sector who want a recognised qualification
entry: A related qualification at MQF Level 4, such as the IATA Foundation in Travel and Tourism Diploma; and/or
One 'A' Level or equivalent, with a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3 ('O' Level or equivalent)
Mature students without all the formal qualifications may be considered through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), with an interview

idea.match: Undergraduate Diploma in Applied IT Essentials
idea.overview: A practice-oriented MQF Level 5 diploma that takes learners from everyday digital literacy to the technical skills employers expect in IT roles. Students start with workplace technologies, digital tools and cybersecurity awareness, then move on to programming fundamentals, cloud computing and data management. It suits school leavers and career changers who want a fast, hands-on route into IT.
who: Post-secondary school leavers aiming for an IT career
Working professionals from non-IT backgrounds who want to reskill
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 (one 'A' Level or equivalent in any subject, or a related professional qualification), with a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3
Applicants without all the formal qualifications may be accepted through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), for example with a CV showing relevant IT experience

idea.overview: An MQF Level 5 diploma in the business of hospitality: hotels, restaurants, wellness centres, cruises and tourism services. Students cover operations, finance, health and safety, customer care, supervisory and HR skills, and consumer behaviour, along with innovation and current issues in the industry. It prepares students for supervisory roles in a fast-growing sector.
who: People seeking academic and professional advancement in hospitality
Professionals returning to work or changing career
modules: An Introduction to Finance and Cashier
Supervisory and HR Skills for Hospitality Professionals
Communication Skills and Work Ethics for Hospitality
Consumer Behaviour and Marketing in Hospitality
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 (one 'A' Level or equivalent in any subject), and a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3
Preference is given to applicants with one year of work experience related to the programme

idea.src: pp. 92-93 (interim exit award of the Undergraduate Higher Diploma in Management)
idea.overview: A one-year MQF Level 5 management diploma made up of the first five modules of IDEA College's Undergraduate Higher Diploma in Management. It builds academic and digital literacy, critical thinking and research skills, then introduces work psychology and the foundations of management and organisational behaviour. Students can continue to the Higher Diploma (120 ECTS) and on to the Bachelor of Science in Management.
who: People building fundamental management knowledge
Employees moving from first-level supervisory roles towards management
modules: Work Psychology: Emotional and Social Intelligence
Foundations of Management and Organisational Behaviour
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 (one 'A' Level or equivalent in any subject), and a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3 ('O' Level or equivalent)
careers: Supervisory roles in business, public administration, retail, finance and hospitality
A first step towards higher managerial roles

idea.match: Undergraduate Diploma in Supply Chain Management and Logistics
idea.src: pp. 76-77 (interim exit award of the Undergraduate Higher Diploma in Supply Chain Management and Logistics)
idea.overview: A one-year MQF Level 5 diploma made up of the first ten modules of IDEA College's Undergraduate Higher Diploma in Supply Chain Management and Logistics. It covers how goods and information flow between suppliers, manufacturers, logistics providers, retailers and consumers, from procurement and demand management to warehousing, global logistics and shipping documentation. Students can continue to the full Higher Diploma (120 ECTS).
who: People seeking a career in supply chain management and logistics
Professionals returning to work or changing career
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 (one 'A' Level or equivalent in any subject), and a pass in English and Mathematics at MQF Level 3
Preference is given to applicants with one year of related work experience; equivalent qualifications from abroad are considered
careers: Roles in procurement, warehousing and distribution

idea.match: Bachelor Degree (Honours) in Tourism and Hospitality Management
idea.overview: A three-year MQF Level 6 honours degree combining hospitality operations with tourism management. Students study hospitality operations, finance, health and safety, customer care, supervision and consumer behaviour, then tourism principles, travel geography, event management, sustainable and niche tourism, and tourism and hospitality law. A project and a dissertation build research skills for management careers across the industry.
who: People seeking to advance their knowledge of tourism and hospitality management
Those aiming for management careers across the tourism and hospitality industry
modules: Consumer Behaviour and Marketing in Hospitality
Tourism and Hospitality Law and Policy
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 (one 'A' Level or equivalent in any subject), and a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3
Applicants without all the formal qualifications may be considered through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), with an interview

idea.overview: A three-year MQF Level 6 computing degree covering mathematics, programming, data analytics, software development, computer systems, networks, web development and databases. In the second year students choose a specialisation in digital marketing, blockchain or intelligent systems, and the final year adds machine learning, security, the Internet of Things and a dissertation.
who: Students seeking academic and professional advancement in computing
Professionals returning to work or changing career into IT
modules: Specialisation: Digital Marketing, Blockchain or Intelligent Systems
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 in subjects related to Mathematics, Science or Computing (minimum two 'A' Levels or equivalent), and a pass in English ('O' Level or equivalent)
Preference is given to applicants with a Level 4 diploma in engineering or computing and A-level standard mathematics

idea.overview: A three-year MQF Level 6 honours degree in travel and tourism. Year one lays the foundations in tourism, hospitality management, travel geography and destination management, year two adds tourism business management, event management, tourism marketing and a project, and the final year covers sustainable and niche tourism, tourism law and policy, cross-cultural communication and a dissertation. Interim awards are available after modules 1-3 (certificate) and 1-6 (diploma).
who: People seeking to advance their knowledge of travel and tourism
Those aiming for a range of careers in the travel and tourism industry
entry: A related qualification at MQF Level 4, such as the IATA Foundation in Travel and Tourism Diploma; and/or
One 'A' Level or equivalent, with a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3
Mature students without all the formal qualifications may be considered through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), with an interview

idea.overview: A three-year MQF Level 6 management degree that builds from management foundations to strategy, governance and data-driven decision-making. The curriculum blends leadership, economics, operations, marketing, research and analytics, with emphasis on emotional intelligence, digital transformation, ethical governance and sustainability, and ends with a research dissertation.
who: People seeking a first-cycle (undergraduate) degree in management
Those aiming for careers in business administration, marketing, HR, operations, entrepreneurship or project management
modules: Foundations of Management and Organisational Behaviour
Innovation, Technology, and the Future of Work
entry: A qualification at MQF Level 4 (one 'A' Level or equivalent in any subject), and a pass in English Language and Mathematics at MQF Level 3 ('O' Level or equivalent)
Applicants without all the formal qualifications may be considered through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), with an interview
careers: Director, in private or public organisations

idea.overview: An MQF Level 7 master's for managers who want to build strategy, policy and leadership skills to master's level. Core modules cover managing organisations and people, operations, finance and research methods, after which students choose electives and can follow a specialisation such as project management, marketing or innovation. The degree also strengthens progression to doctoral study.
who: Managers with supervisory or middle-management experience
Operations, finance, supply chain, retail, marketing and services managers
modules: Project Management or Marketing Management electives
entry: A Level 6 degree and three years' work experience; or
A Level 5 diploma or higher diploma and five years' work experience in a supervisory or managerial role
careers: Director, in private or public organisations

idea.overview: An MQF Level 7 MBA for professionals moving into strategic management and leadership. Eleven compulsory modules cover management and organisational behaviour, finance, accounting and economics, operations and analytics, marketing strategy, corporate strategy, negotiation and crisis management, information management and the global economy, followed by a final project.
who: Emerging leaders and mid-career managers
Experienced practitioners moving into strategic leadership
entry: A Level 6 degree; or
A related Level 5 diploma or higher diploma and four years of relevant work experience, subject to interview by the Admissions Board

idea.match: Master of Science (M.Sc.) in Elderly Care Management
idea.overview: An MQF Level 7 master's for current and future managers of elderly care services, one of the fastest-growing parts of healthcare. It draws on management, policy, law and the social and behavioural sciences, covering leadership, quality improvement, finance and HR in care settings, the ageing process, palliative care and the psychology of old age.
who: Care home managers and directors
Professionals in community, social, health and long-term care services for older people
modules: Public Policy and Legal Basis for Elderly Care Management
Welfare and Economic Issues in Elderly Care
Managing Institutions and HR for Elderly Care
Quality Management and Elderly Care Service Improvement
Financial Management of Elderly Care Settings
Critical Appraisal of the Ageing Process
Palliative and End of Life Care
Psychology and Psychiatry of Old Age
entry: A Level 6 degree and three years' work experience; or
A Level 5 diploma or higher diploma and five years' work experience in a related role
careers: Elderly care home manager or director
Chief executive or financial officer of an elderly care organisation

idea.match: Master of Science in Healthcare Management and Leadership
idea.overview: An MQF Level 7 master's that prepares healthcare professionals for senior leadership. It brings management, leadership, strategy and operations together with the realities of healthcare systems, covering finance, economics, quality, patient care, ICT and intercultural management, and closes with an independent dissertation.
who: Healthcare professionals moving into management
Professionals from other sectors transitioning into healthcare leadership
modules: ICT and Information Systems in Healthcare
entry: A Level 6 degree and two years' work experience; or
A Level 5 diploma or higher diploma and five years' work experience in a supervisory or managerial role

idea.match: Master of Science in Hospitality Management
idea.overview: An MQF Level 7 master's for hospitality professionals moving into senior leadership. It combines advanced business management with hospitality practice, covering operations, revenue management, marketing and events, finance, people leadership, health, safety and crisis management, and gastronomy, and ends with a dissertation.
who: Hospitality professionals with supervisory or middle-management experience
Event, restaurant, reception, guest services and housekeeping managers
modules: The Art and Science of Gastronomy
Health, Safety and Crisis Management in Hospitality
entry: A Level 6 degree and three years' work experience; or
A Level 5 diploma or higher diploma and five years' work experience in a supervisory or managerial role
careers: Senior posts such as head of department or events director in hotels, restaurants, casinos and other hospitality organisations

idea.match: Master of Science in Public Health
idea.overview: An MQF Level 7 master's made up of seven modules and a dissertation, aligned with the UK Faculty of Public Health Diplomate Examination (DFPH) syllabus and the European Agency of Public Health Education Accreditation (APHEA). It covers the principles of public health, epidemiology and statistics, evaluation, disease causation and prevention, health information, and the social, policy and economic influences on health.
who: People advancing their knowledge of public health
Those aiming for careers in public health practice, policy or research
modules: Research Methods - Epidemiology and Statistical Methods
Research Methods - Assessment and Evaluation Approaches
Medical Sociology, Social Policy, and Health Economics
Organisation and Management of Healthcare Programmes
entry: A Level 6 degree related to public health; or
An unrelated Level 6 degree and at least one year of relevant experience (subject to interview); or
A related Level 5 diploma or higher diploma and two years of related work experience (subject to interview)

doria.title: Healthcare and Social Care Courses in Italy
doria.overview: Fondazione Doria's healthcare and social care stream trains students for care roles in Italy, from personal care and home care to childcare, community support and healthcare administration. It includes the Social and Healthcare Operator (OSS) and Social Care Operator (OSA) programmes. Training is practical, and employers in the sector host the professional internship stage.
highlights: Social and Healthcare Operator (OSS) and Social Care Operator (OSA)
Care for older people, people with disabilities and children
Healthcare administration, reception and booking roles

doria.title: Construction and Technical Trades Courses in Italy
doria.overview: The construction and technical trades stream builds practical skills for in-demand building and installation jobs in Italy. It covers site trades such as bricklaying, carpentry, plastering, tiling, scaffolding and welding, and technical roles in electrical, plumbing, air-conditioning and refrigeration systems, CAD drafting and site supervision.
highlights: Building trades: bricklayer, carpenter, plasterer, tiler, painter, scaffolder, welder
Systems technicians: electrical, plumbing and heating, air-conditioning, refrigeration
CAD technical drafting and construction site technician

doria.title: Hospitality, Tourism and Culinary Courses in Italy
doria.overview: The hospitality, tourism and culinary stream prepares students for kitchens, dining rooms, bars, hotels and tourism services in Italy. Courses range from cook, pastry chef, pizza maker and baker to waiter, bartender, sommelier and barista, as well as hotel reception, housekeeping, event organisation and tourism planning.
highlights: Culinary: cook, professional chef, pastry chef, pizza maker, baker, ice cream maker
Food and beverage service: waiter, head waiter, bartender, barista, sommelier
Hotels and tourism: reception, housekeeping, event organiser, tourism services

doria.title: Fashion, Beauty and Personal Care Courses in Italy
doria.overview: The fashion, beauty and personal care stream covers tailoring, clothing manufacturing, beauty and aesthetics, and hairdressing and styling. Practical training uses working salon stations and professional equipment.

doria.title: IT, Digital and Automation Courses in Italy
doria.overview: The IT, digital and automation stream trains students in the technologies behind modern business and Industry 4.0. It spans IT support, networking, software and web development, cybersecurity and data, digital marketing and e-commerce, and industrial automation, PLC and SCADA programming, robotics and smart manufacturing.
highlights: IT support, networking, software and web development
Cybersecurity, data analysis, cloud computing and artificial intelligence
Industrial automation, PLC, SCADA, robotics and smart manufacturing
